solution: Put \(t = 1 + \sin 6x\), so that \(dt = 6\cos 6x\, dx\). Therefore \(\int \cos 6x\sqrt{1+\sin 6x}\, dx = \frac{1}{6}\int t^{\frac{1}{2}}\, dt = \frac{1}{6}\times\frac{2}{3}(t)^{\frac{3}{2}} + C = \frac{1}{9}(1+\sin 6x)^{\frac{3}{2}} + C\).

We have \(\int \frac{(x^4 - x)^{\frac{1}{4}}}{x^5}\, dx = \int \frac{\left(1 - \frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}}{x^4}\, dx\). Put \(1 - \frac{1}{x^3} = 1 - x^{-3} = t\), so that \(\frac{3}{x^4}\, dx = dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{(x^4 - x)^{\frac{1}{4}}}{x^5}\, dx = \frac{1}{3}\int t^{\frac{1}{4}}\, dt = \frac{1}{3}\times\frac{4}{5} t^{\frac{5}{4}} + C = \frac{4}{15}\left(1 - \frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{\frac{5}{4}} + C\).

By division, \(\frac{x^4}{(x-1)(x^2+1)} = (x+1) + \frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}\). Now express \(\frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}\). So \(1 = A(x^2+1) + (Bx+C)(x-1)\). Equating coefficients gives \(A + B = 0,\; C - B = 0,\; A - C = 1\), which give \(A = \frac{1}{2},\; B = C = -\frac{1}{2}\). Hence \(\frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)} = \frac{1}{2(x-1)} - \frac{1}{2}\frac{x}{x^2+1} - \frac{1}{2(x^2+1)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^4}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}\, dx = \frac{x^2}{2} + x + \frac{1}{2}\log|x-1| - \frac{1}{4}\log(x^2+1) - \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x + C\).
_note: The book prints the denominator as (x-1)(x^2+x+1) in the intermediate 'substituting (3) in (1)' and 'Therefore' lines; the correct denominator per the example statement is (x-1)(x^2+1) — used here.

solution: Let \(I = \int \left[\log(\log x) + \frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\right] dx = \int \log(\log x)\, dx + \int \frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\, dx\). In the first integral, take 1 as the second function and integrate by parts: \(I = x\log(\log x) - \int \frac{1}{x\log x} x\, dx + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2} = x\log(\log x) - \int \frac{dx}{\log x} + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2}\) ... (1). Again, consider \(\int \frac{dx}{\log x}\), take 1 as the second function and integrate by parts: \(\int \frac{dx}{\log x} = \frac{x}{\log x} - \int x\left\{-\frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\cdot\frac{1}{x}\right\} dx = \frac{x}{\log x} + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2}\) ... (2). Putting (2) in (1), \(I = x\log(\log x) - \frac{x}{\log x} - \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2} + \int \frac{dx}{(\log x)^2} = x\log(\log x) - \frac{x}{\log x} + C\).

We have \(I = \int \left[\sqrt{\cot x} + \sqrt{\tan x}\right] dx = \int \sqrt{\tan x}\,(1 + \cot x)\, dx\). Put \(\tan x = t^2\), so that \(\sec^2 x\, dx = 2t\, dt\), or \(dx = \frac{2t\, dt}{1+t^4}\). Then \(I = \int t\left(1 + \frac{1}{t^2}\right)\frac{2t}{1+t^4}\, dt = 2\int \frac{t^2+1}{t^4+1}\, dt = 2\int \frac{\left(1+\frac{1}{t^2}\right)dt}{\left(t - \frac{1}{t}\right)^2 + 2}\). Put \(t - \frac{1}{t} = y\), so that \(\left(1 + \frac{1}{t^2}\right)dt = dy\). Then \(I = 2\int \frac{dy}{y^2 + (\sqrt 2)^2} = \sqrt 2\,\tan^{-1}\frac{y}{\sqrt 2} + C = \sqrt 2\,\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{t^2-1}{\sqrt 2\, t}\right) + C = \sqrt 2\,\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan x - 1}{\sqrt{2\tan x}}\right) + C\).

Let \(I = \int \frac{\sin 2x \cos 2x}{\sqrt{9 - \cos^4 2x}}\, dx\). Put \(\cos^2(2x) = t\) so that \(4\sin 2x \cos 2x\, dx = -dt\). Therefore \(I = -\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{9 - t^2}} = -\frac{1}{4}\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{t}{3}\right) + C = -\frac{1}{4}\sin^{-1}\left[\frac{1}{3}\cos^2 2x\right] + C\).

solution: Here \(f(x) = |x\sin\pi x| = \begin{cases} x\sin\pi x & \text{for } -1 \le x \le 1 \\ -x\sin\pi x & \text{for } 1 \le x \le \frac{3}{2} \end{cases}\). Therefore \(\int_{-1}^{\frac{3}{2}} |x\sin\pi x|\, dx = \int_{-1}^{1} x\sin\pi x\, dx + \int_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}} -x\sin\pi x\, dx = \int_{-1}^{1} x\sin\pi x\, dx - \int_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}} x\sin\pi x\, dx\). Integrating by parts, \(\int_{-1}^{\frac{3}{2}} |x\sin\pi x|\, dx = \left[\frac{-x\cos\pi x}{\pi} + \frac{\sin\pi x}{\pi^2}\right]_{-1}^{1} - \left[\frac{-x\cos\pi x}{\pi} + \frac{\sin\pi x}{\pi^2}\right]_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}} = \frac{2}{\pi} - \left[-\frac{1}{\pi^2} - \frac{1}{\pi}\right] = \frac{3}{\pi} + \frac{1}{\pi^2}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{x\, dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x} = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{(\pi - x)\, dx}{a^2\cos^2(\pi-x) + b^2\sin^2(\pi-x)}\) (using \(P_4\)) \(= \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x} - I\). Thus \(2I = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x}\), or \(I = \frac{\pi}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x} = \frac{\pi}{2}\cdot 2\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x}\) (using \(P_6\)) \(= \pi\left[\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\frac{\sec^2 x\, dx}{a^2 + b^2\tan^2 x} + \int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\csc^2 x\, dx}{a^2\cot^2 x + b^2}\right]\). Putting \(\tan x = t\) and \(\cot x = u\), \(I = \pi\left[\int_{0}^{1}\frac{dt}{a^2 + b^2 t^2} - \int_{1}^{0}\frac{du}{a^2 u^2 + b^2}\right] = \frac{\pi}{ab}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{bt}{a}\right]_{0}^{1} - \frac{\pi}{ab}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{au}{b}\right]_{1}^{0} = \frac{\pi}{ab}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{b}{a} + \tan^{-1}\frac{a}{b}\right] = \frac{\pi^2}{2ab}\).
